name: Mikoko Pamoja (Mangrove Blue Carbon), Kenya
monitoring_objective: Verify protection, restoration, and permanence vs the certified project design.

disclosure.title: Mikoko Pamoja: Plan Vivo Blue-Carbon Certification & Impact Claims
disclosure.issuer: Mikoko Pamoja Community Organisation (MPCO), coordinated by ACES
disclosure.summary: World's first community-led blue-carbon project. Plan Vivo project design promises protection of standing mangrove, active restoration, and permanence of the carbon stock, the outcomes a small community entity must prove to keep issuing credits and unlock finance.

observation_series.note: Baseline NDVI 0.404 at the start of the 2019-2024 analysis window; dense mangrove, no clearing.
NDVI 0.63 - within the interannual range (std 0.093); mangrove extent stable, no clearing.
NDVI 0.476; 2019-2024 slope -0.012/yr, within interannual variability - no significant change; 0 deforestation vs the ~2.7%/yr regional baseline.

cross_check.observed: Canopy extent stable across 2016-2024; about 0% loss vs the ~2.7%/yr regional deforestation baseline.

Not resolvable from satellite: ~0.4 ha/yr replanting is below Sentinel-2 resolution. NDVI is flat (slope -0.012/yr, no significant change) and 0 deforestation - permanence verified, but the specific 10 ha restoration cannot be independently confirmed.
cross_check.variance: not satellite-resolvable (permanence verified; the 10 ha gain is not measurable from Earth observation)

cross_check.observed: Permanence VERIFIED (extent stable 2016-2024, 0 clearing). Our standing-stock estimate ~8,668 tCO2e [2,300-8,800] (AGB, Tier-1) is a DIFFERENT quantity from the 9,880 credited tCO2e (an avoided-deforestation flux) - we verify permanence, not the credit counterfactual.

confidence.rationale: Satellite is the sole source. Over 2019-2024 the mangrove NDVI is stable (slope -0.012/yr, within interannual variability; 39% gain / 4% loss, no significant loss) and no deforestation is detected - permanence consistent. Physical risk is Low (composite 5/100): the engine's worst hazard is flood at 0.093 m 100-yr depth (4.6% depth-damage), with fire 4 and degradation 4. Standing-stock carbon is an above-ground-only lower bound of ~8,668 tCO2e (ESA CCI, 28.3 t/ha AGB) over the 177.5 ha analysis AOI; the issuer's 9,880 tCO2e credited is a separate avoided-deforestation flux, not a stock. Screening: partially consistent - no loss observed, but the credit counterfactual is not satellite-measurable. Note: the automated flood proxy may under-rate tidal inundation (disclosed limitation), but the score is reported as the engine computes it, not manually adjusted.
drivers: NDVI stable 2019-2024 (slope -0.012/yr, within noise); 39% gain / 4% loss - no significant loss (Sentinel-2)
Physical risk Low (composite 5/100): worst hazard flood 0.093 m 100-yr depth -> 4.6% depth-damage (Aqueduct + JRC/Huizinga); fire 4, degradation 4
Carbon = above-ground-only lower bound ~8,668 tCO2e (ESA CCI, 28.3 t/ha AGB) over the 177.5 ha AOI; distinct from the 9,880 tCO2e credited avoided-deforestation flux
AOI is a 177.5 ha analysis box, larger than the ~117 ha certified project - read as 'region analysed', not exact footprint

limitations: confirms canopy extent/change, not species composition
carbon is an NDVI-biomass proxy, not MRV-grade metering
community-benefit figure is issuer-reported, not satellite-observable
evidence.financial_relevance: Canopy protection and growth indicator relevant to credit-issuance monitoring.

limitations: high-resolution basemap timelapse for visual context; the basemap refresh date lags real events, so it is not the dated capture each observation was measured from
shows canopy stability to the eye; the NDVI/permanence measurements come from the Sentinel observation series
evidence.financial_relevance: A dated high-resolution timelapse of the AOI (Esri World Imagery Wayback): visual confirmation that the mangrove canopy is stable, with no clearing, alongside the measured evidence.
